h1: The 5 Best Leaf Blowers for Large Yards of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Large Yard Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five leaf blowers for large yards, from backpack gas models to a cordless handheld, compared on airflow and carry style.
summary: The Echo X Series backpack blower tops the list on airflow, at 1110 CFM. The PROYAMA offers 880 CFM in a backpack gas model for less money, the Husqvarna 150BT is a mid-power backpack, the Husqvarna 360BT is a gas backpack alternative, and the EGO is the cordless handheld.
intro: On a big lot, airflow is only half the story. A handheld that pushes plenty of air still wears your arm out after twenty minutes, which is why backpack models dominate the large-yard category.

We reviewed eight blowers on paper using the spec sheets, comparing airflow in CFM, carry style and fuel type, and ranked the five that best fit a large property. Prices appear as buckets because they move often.

products.name: Echo 220 MPH 1110 CFM 79.9 cc Gas 2-Stroke X Series Backpack Blower
products.verdict: The highest airflow in the group, in a gas backpack frame.
products.description:
The Echo X Series is a gas 2-stroke backpack blower with a 79.9 cc engine, rated at 1110 CFM and 220 MPH. It leads this ranking on raw output.

It ranks above the PROYAMA because its stated airflow is about 230 CFM higher, which matters for wet leaves and large piles. The tradeoff is price: it sits in the $500+ bucket, the most expensive here.

It suits owners of acre-scale properties who clear a lot of debris each fall. The caveat is two-stroke fuel mixing and engine noise.
products.idealFor: Owners of very large properties with heavy leaf fall.
products.skipIf: You want a quiet, low-maintenance electric.

products.name: PROYAMA 72CC Gas Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: An 880 CFM gas backpack for far less money.
products.description:
The PROYAMA is a 72 cc gas backpack blower rated at 880 CFM. It is in the $100-200 bucket, the cheapest backpack here.

It ranks below the Echo because its airflow is lower, but it matches the EGO 880 CFM figure while using a backpack frame that is easier on the arms over a long session.

Choose it if you want large-yard output at a budget price. The caveat is that the spec sheet is thin, so check the listing for noise, vibration and warranty before buying.
products.idealFor: Large-yard owners on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want a full, detailed spec sheet.

products.name: EGO Power+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A cordless handheld that reaches 880 CFM.
products.description:
This EGO Power+ is a cordless electric handheld rated at 880 CFM. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks below the PROYAMA on cost for the same airflow, but trades fuel and noise for a battery. The tradeoff is carry style, since a handheld tires you faster than a backpack frame.

It suits owners who want gas-class airflow without fuel mixing. The caveat is that the listing facts here give no runtime, so check battery capacity for your yard size.
products.idealFor: Owners who want gas-level air without gas upkeep.
products.skipIf: You clear a full acre in one session.

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A backpack gas blower at 765 CFM from a known brand.
products.description:
The Husqvarna 150BT is a gas backpack blower rated at 765 CFM, in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks fourth because it has about 115 CFM less than the PROYAMA at a higher price.

It suits a mid-sized yard where 765 CFM is enough. The caveat is that it costs more than the PROYAMA for less airflow.
products.idealFor: Mid-sized yards where 765 CFM is enough.
products.skipIf: You want the most airflow per dollar.

products.name: Husqvarna 360BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A gas backpack option, though the spec sheet is sparse.
products.description:
The Husqvarna 360BT is a gas backpack blower in the $200-500 bucket. The facts available list the backpack style but no airflow figure.

It ranks last because without a stated CFM we cannot place it against the others on output, which is the key spec for a big yard.

It suits buyers who will confirm airflow on the manufacturer page. The caveat is exactly that missing number.
products.idealFor: Buyers who will verify airflow first.
products.skipIf: You pick on a published CFM number.

whatMatters.detail: CFM measures the volume of air a blower moves each minute. More CFM clears wet or heavy leaves faster across a big lawn. Look for the number in the title or spec list rather than relying on a marketing claim like powerful.
A backpack frame moves the weight to your back and hips. On a large yard this decides whether you can finish in one go. Check the listing for the carry style.
Gas gives long runtime but needs fuel and makes noise, while cordless is quieter but limited by battery. For a large yard, runtime matters. Look for the battery capacity or engine size.
Engine displacement in cc hints at power and fuel use. A 72 cc or 79.9 cc engine is large for a blower. Compare it with the stated CFM for a sanity check.
A listing with no airflow or weight is harder to judge. Missing numbers are a red flag. Cross-check against the manufacturer page before you buy.

faq.q: What CFM do I need for a large yard?
faq.a: More is better on large lots. The picks here range from 765 to 1110 CFM. Wet leaves call for the higher end.

faq.q: Is a gas blower worth it over cordless?
faq.a: For long sessions, usually yes, since you are not limited by battery. The EGO is a good option if you want to skip fuel.

faq.q: Do I need to mix fuel?
faq.a: The Echo is a 2-stroke gas engine, which typically uses mixed fuel. Check the manual for the right ratio.

faq.q: Why is the Husqvarna 360BT ranked last?
faq.a: The spec sheet we have gives no airflow figure, so we cannot compare its output. Verify CFM before buying.

faq.q: Can a handheld handle a large yard?
faq.a: The EGO reaches 880 CFM, so output is fine. Fatigue is the bigger issue over long sessions.

faq.q: How do I maintain a gas blower?
faq.a: Use fresh fuel and keep the air filter clean. Store with an empty tank or stabilizer for the off season.

finalTake: The Echo X Series is the best pick for a large property thanks to 1110 CFM in a backpack. The PROYAMA gets you 880 CFM for much less, and the EGO is the choice if you would rather skip gas. The Husqvarnas are worth a look only after you confirm their numbers.
